content:
In May this year, the Google Health app launched alongside a new, affordable lineup of Google Fitbit Air health trackers.

Initially, Google Health only supported one-way integration with Apple Health. The app could read and import health data recorded by the iPhone, Apple Watch, and other HealthKit-connected apps, but was unable to write Fitbit data back to Apple Health.

An update to the Google Health iOS app today closes that missing gap.

Google Health can now not only read data from HealthKit but also write information to Apple Health.

The release notes for version 5.05 specifically highlight the Apple Health sync feature:

Workout records, sleep, vitals, steps, and other Fitbit data can now be shared with other HealthKit-compatible apps, subject to the permissions selected by the user.

Before this year, users wanting to import Fitbit data into Apple Health generally had to go through third-party sync tools or make indirect connections via other services.

This gap can be traced back as far as 2014. Shortly after Apple launched HealthKit in iOS 8, Fitbit said it had no intention of supporting the platform.

Version 5.05 also adds a new “Smart Health Links” feature, allowing users to share medical records with healthcare professionals or family members.

The new version of the Google Health iOS app is now available on the App Store. For more information about Google Health, visit 9to5Google.
